miniProject.title: Restartable decoder training with retained failure evidence
miniProject.brief: Extend `lmlab` with a reliable single-device trainer for the tested decoder and versioned corpus. Use the pinned nanoGPT path and PyTorch from the units, prove updates and recovery before the bounded study, and retain numerical, data and performance incidents without claiming fleet reliability.
steps: Adapt the pinned nanoGPT trainer in `train/` to your decoder. Check masked token accumulation against concatenated-batch gradients, including uneven, partial and empty windows; pass CS336 Assignment 1 AdamW tests and retain scalar-update, tied-group, moment-resume and actual update-ratio audits before training.

Save a decoder-specific muP worksheet, actual group multipliers and bounded initialization-transfer scales against the stated parameterization rules. Check accumulation, unscaling and clipping against full-precision updates; inject a nonfinite event and retain refused-update, unchanged-moment and precision-state restoration regressions with preceding diagnostics.

Freeze the baseline contract in `registry/`, binding code, dependencies, data, tokenizer, model, objective, optimizer, precision and evaluator. Gate launches on deterministic trace equality and a separate learnable-batch overfit diagnostic; retain fixed held-out evaluation and budget, identity-mismatch, stop and rollback tests.

Extend nanoGPT's checkpoint path with a state inventory covering model, moments, groups, schedule, scaler, counters, RNG, loader, prefetch and callbacks. Publish immutable payloads with integrity manifests; test killed writers and corruption against acceptance rules, retaining explicit last-good fallback without claiming power-loss durability.

Compare uninterrupted training with killed-process continuation under dropout, checking batches, losses, updates and complete state against the deterministic CPU reference. Retain missing-RNG, repeated-shard and strict data/tokenizer/config fingerprint negative controls, first-discontinuity evidence and the declared numerical or statistical equivalence boundary.

Fork stable-phase state into constant and cooldown schedules and compare token batches under equal learning-rate search budgets. Hold tokens, held-out evaluation and paired seeds fixed; retain losses, uncertainty, exposure, attempted/successful updates and shared, marginal and all-attempt costs. Reproduce the baseline from clean state.

Instrument phase timelines, per-source losses and layer scales; localize injected numerical and input-wait incidents against unchanged-batch replays. Reconcile dtype-specific state-memory and operation predictions with profiles, retaining pre-event history, throughput, observer overhead, first-invalid evidence, repaired regressions, an incident index and bounded, single-device recovery claims.
deliverables: The `train/` trainer, complete-state inventory, immutable checkpoints and objective, precision, publication and killed-process resume regressions.
Frozen baseline and schedule/batch studies with fixed evaluation, update ledgers, paired uncertainty and all attempts retained.
Incident index, matched replays, profiling reconciliations and clean baseline reproduction instructions with explicit recovery and hardware-scope limits.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 1 AdamW regression tests
checks.note: Pass the optimizer regression; add masked accumulation, parameter-group, precision and complete-state continuation tests in your trainer.

rubric.pass: Your masked gradient and scalar AdamW oracles pass before training; group identities, width multipliers and precision state are audited. Deterministic launch, learnable-batch, stop and nonfinite-refusal tests pass.
rubric.strong: A wrong denominator or clipping order fails a targeted regression, and the repaired update agrees with the independent full-precision control.

rubric.pass: Your killed-writer and corruption tests reject uncommitted state without live mutation. Dropout continuation matches the uninterrupted reference; missing-RNG, repeated-shard and fingerprint controls fail, with last-good recovery explicit.
rubric.strong: Fresh-process state comparisons localize the earliest differing owner, including a pending batch; a clean baseline rerun reproduces the documented recovery contract.

rubric.pass: Matched schedule and batch studies retain paired-seed outcomes and all costs. Timeline and memory/operation reconciliations, incident histories, matched replays and regressions support bounded diagnoses rather than hardware-fault assertions.
rubric.strong: An input-wait repair preserves updates and resume behavior; separate clean timings expose observer overhead, and the negative regime changes the next experiment.

miniProject.feedsInto: Complete checkpoints, deterministic exposure, schedules and all-attempt ledgers feed scaling, adaptation and real-code integration. Resume regressions, failure postmortems and measured resource residuals become the capstone's reproducible baseline and recovery evidence.
